title: Beck–Fiala conjecture
formal: Is there a real constant \(C>0\) such that for every three integers \(m,n,t\ge1\) and every matrix \(A\in\{0,1\}^{m\times n}\) with \(\sum_{i=1}^m A_{ij}\le t\) for each column \(j\), there exists a single vector \(x\in\{-1,1\}^n\) satisfying \[\max_{1\le i\le m}\left|\sum_{j=1}^n A_{ij}x_j\right|\le C\sqrt t?\] The same constant must work for every dimension, frequency bound and matrix.
definitions: The underlying elements are \(1,\ldots,n\), and the \(i\)-th set is \(S_i=\{j:A_{ij}=1\}\). The ordered collection \((S_1,\ldots,S_m)\) may contain repeated or empty sets, and some elements may occur in no set. Each element is in at most \(t\) sets, counting repeated rows separately. This is a restriction on column sums, not on the cardinality of each set, the number of elements or the number of sets. The integer \(t\) is an allowed upper bound on frequency; it need not be attained or be at most \(m\). A two-coloring assigns each element exactly one sign \(x_j\in\{-1,1\}\). The imbalance of a set is the absolute difference between the numbers of its plus and minus elements, equal to \(|\sum_{j\in S_i}x_j|\). Define \(\operatorname{disc}(A)=\min_{x\in\{-1,1\}^n}\max_{1\le i\le m}|\sum_j A_{ij}x_j|\); the minimum exists because the set of complete colorings is finite. One coloring must control all sets simultaneously. The conjecture is the existence of some universal finite constant, with no requirement to minimize it. The coloring may depend on the entire matrix; no online order, random input distribution or efficient construction requirement is imposed. Every element is colored, and no fractional or partially unassigned coloring is a witness. Dimensions and \(t\) are positive; a zero-frequency matrix is still allowed and has discrepancy zero.

context_blocks.text: A coloring partitions the elements into two classes while trying to divide every set evenly. The conjecture permits large sets and arbitrarily many constraints: only the participation of each individual element is bounded. Writing \(y=(\mathbf 1+x)/2\in\{0,1\}^n\), where \(\mathbf 1\) is the all-one vector, gives \(A(y-\mathbf 1/2)=Ax/2\). Hence a discrepancy bound also bounds the simultaneous error of rounding the all-one-half vector. This identity explains the optimization connection without adding a rounding algorithm to the target.

Beck and Fiala’s 1981 theorem gives discrepancy at most \(2t-1\), uniformly in the two matrix dimensions. Known examples require discrepancy of order \(\sqrt t\), so the conjecture proposes the correct order in frequency up to a constant. Bansal and Jiang recall these facts in §1; their review of the older Banaszczyk bound gives \(O(\sqrt{t\log n})\), which still depends on the number of elements.

The Komlós conjecture allows arbitrary real matrices whose individual columns have Euclidean norm at most one and asks for constant discrepancy. Scaling a Beck–Fiala matrix by \(1/\sqrt t\) makes it admissible for Komlós, since the squared Euclidean norm of a column becomes its number of ones divided by \(t\). A Komlós constant therefore implies the same Beck–Fiala constant. The reverse implication is not asserted; the general real-matrix question has a wider domain.

Bansal and Jiang’s Theorem 1.3 gives the square-root bound once \(t\) is at least a constant multiple of \((\log n)^2\), and Theorem 1.4 gives \(\widetilde O(\sqrt t+\sqrt{\log n})\) in the full range, with powers of \(\log\log n\) suppressed. Their 2025 preprint was followed by STOC 2026. The first result restricts the frequency range; the second retains growth in \(n\). Neither of these statements alone yields the uniform target.

Altschuler and Tikhomirov’s July 2026 Corollary 1.2 states that for each fixed \(\eta>0\), constants \(a_\eta,b_\eta>0\) and \(N_\eta\) exist such that \(\operatorname{disc}(A)\le b_\eta\sqrt t\) when \(n\ge N_\eta\) and \(t\ge a_\eta(\log n)(\log\log n)^{2+\eta}\). Here \(n\) is the number of elements, denoted \(T\) in that source, and the logs are natural. Its stronger online result chooses signs irrevocably as columns arrive and bounds every prefix for a sequence fixed in advance. The card instead asks only for a complete final coloring chosen with the whole input available. The preprint’s proof was not independently verified in this review.

Guo, Fang and Lu’s preprint submitted on 10 September 2026 claims the full statement: Corollary 1.2 gives \(\operatorname{disc}(A)<3\sqrt{2\pi t}\) for every allowed positive \(m,n,t\), with no frequency threshold. It follows there from their claimed Komlós theorem. This is an affirmative claim matching the exact card target, not another range-restricted improvement. The authors make no polynomial-time implementation claim. This review checked the statement and parameter match, but did not independently verify the complete new proof, so the scientific status is uncertain.

why: The conjecture asks whether a local bound on how many constraints involve one element controls the error of balancing all constraints by the square root of that frequency. It is a central sparsity question in discrepancy theory, with a direct interpretation as simultaneously rounding half-integral choices in many overlapping constraints.
answer_criterion: Supply a complete mathematically correct proof checked in Lean of the universal bound, or a Lean-checked proof of its logical negation: for every real \(C>0\), there exist positive integers \(m,n,t\) and a binary matrix \(A\) with every column sum at most \(t\), such that for every \(x\in\{-1,1\}^n\) there exists a row \(i\) with \(|\sum_j A_{ij}x_j|>C\sqrt t\). Thus a refutation establishes that \(\operatorname{disc}(A)/\sqrt t\) is unbounded over the stated instances. A fixed example with positive discrepancy, or a lower bound proportional to \(\sqrt t\), is consistent with the conjecture. A positive proof must use one constant independent of all parameters; constants depending on \(t\) or bounds restricted to a growing-frequency range do not settle the target. An unverified announced proof, experimental signing search or result conditional on an unproved conjecture is insufficient for Lean benchmark acceptance. No optimal numerical constant or construction-time bound is requested.

progress.text: The classical bound \(2t-1\) is uniform over dimensions, as recalled in the inspected Bansal–Jiang introduction.
Bansal and Jiang obtain \(O(\sqrt t)\) for \(t\) at least a constant multiple of \((\log n)^2\), and a further all-range bound still involving \(n\). The extended abstract appears at STOC 2026.

Altschuler and Tikhomirov’s preprint extends the stated offline square-root bound to \(t\ge a_\eta(\log n)(\log\log n)^{2+\eta}\) for sufficiently large \(n\) and each fixed \(\eta>0\), via a stronger online result.

Guo, Fang and Lu claim the unrestricted bound \(3\sqrt{2\pi t}\) in Corollary 1.2. The claim matches the full target, but the new proof is not independently verified here; the card remains active with uncertain status.

sentences: The Beck–Fiala conjecture asks whether bounded participation of each element in a set system guarantees a coloring with square-root imbalance in every set.
If each element belongs to at most t sets, one complete assignment of signs must achieve imbalance at most a universal constant times the square root of t.
The constant must work for every number of elements and sets, with no lower restriction on t or requirement for an efficient algorithm.
The question is a central sparsity principle for simultaneous rounding and is implied by the more general Komlós conjecture.
A complete Lean proof must establish the universal bound or unbounded normalized discrepancy; a 10 September 2026 preprint claims the full positive bound, with its proof unverified in this review.
